alignments.note: Imperative.
Preposition to unto.
Construct noun with the supplied the, the rectum being an anarthrous proper name (rule 29).
Nomen rectum carries the of (rule 19).
Noun with the indefinite article, which belongs to the noun (rule 15).
Disjunctive particle to or; no correlative pair is written.
Noun.
כִּי takes the ASV's When (rule 55); the unit is discontinuous from its clause by English order (rule 25).
Verb with its auxiliary.
Partitive מִן left with no English word (rule 40); the any answers to the present כֹּל.
כֹּל is what the determiner any renders (rule 15).
Noun.
The ASV writes no the for this article, the rectum being recast as a relative clause (rule 29).

The rectum keeps its own lexeme men together with the relative that, which is the English relational expression the construct licenses (rule 19), exactly as the to of חֲמַס אֶרֶץ → violence done to the land stays with the dependent. The unit is discontinuous around the supplied verb (rule 25). Competing reading: give that men commit whole to הָאָדָם; rejected under rule 20's lexical-verb boundary.

commit is a supplied lexical verb inside a nominal recasting of the construct relation, and no source verb licenses it: the clause's one עָשָׂה is already rendered shall commit. This is rule 20's חֲמַס אֶרֶץ → violence done to the land, where done is added because it predicates an event rather than naming the thing. Competing reading: mark the relative that added with it as one supplied clause; rejected because the construct relation licenses the relational word itself.
Purpose לְ before an infinitive rendered by the connective so as to (rules 52, 30).
Infinitive keeps the verb.
Cognate accusative rendered once with the verb (rule 22).
Preposition to against.
Divine name.
Waw to and.
Verb with auxiliaries, headed on the lexical predicate (rule 24).
No the is written for this article; the demonstrative answers to the present הִוא (rules 15, 47).
Noun.
Agreement article on the demonstrative, unrendered (rule 47).
The demonstrative pronoun הִוא is what the ASV's that realizes; a present morpheme takes its English before an article does (rules 15, 18).

review_notes: Corrected: the accepted alignment gave that men commit whole to הָאָדָם under rule 19. Rule 20's lexical-verb boundary inside a nominal recasting reaches this construction — a construct relation licenses the English relational word but not a supplied lexical verb — so commit is now its own added unit and the rectum keeps that men.
The demonstrative that of הַנֶּפֶשׁ הַהִוא is placed on הִוא, leaving both articles unrepresented (rule 18's closing case, matching NUM.5.31).
מִן is unrepresented because the present כֹּל is what the determiner any renders (rule 15).
